prerequisites: It is advisable to take Projects when the student has passed most of the subjects of the degree, which will allow for better training to undertake the tasks proper to a Project in a technical office. It is also recommended to take this subject to consolidate the knowledge aimed at carrying out the Bachelor's Thesis (TFG), so it is recommended to take it before starting the TFG.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to manage information, handle and apply technical specifications and the necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Respect for human rights and those with disabilities, and willingness to eliminate discriminatory factors based on gender, origin, etc.
Knowledge and abilities to organize and manage projects. To know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.

syllabus_topics: Basic aspects and methodology of projects
Morphology of projects and other technical documents
Project evaluation, planning, programming and control
Drafting an engineering project following UNE 157001 standard
Practical sessions on Planning: Use of specific software for project planning, evaluation, and control (e.g., MS Project or similar)
Practical sessions on Budgeting: Use of commercial software for preparing measurements and budgets of projects (e.g., Presto or similar)
teaching_methods: Exposition of theory and general examples
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, students must complete the practical project and achieve a minimum grade of 5 out of 10. They must also obtain at least 5 out of 10 in both the theory exam and the practical exam. If a part is failed in the ordinary call, the grade for approved parts will be saved for the extraordinary call. If a student does not attend a part but passes others in the ordinary call, they will be marked as "Not presented", and the grades for approved parts will be saved for the next call of the academic year. The practical project grade is valid only for the current academic year.
